standard.title: Verb types and processes
standard.description: understand how verbs represent different processes for doing, feeling, thinking, saying and relating
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand how nouns extend into noun groups and verbs into verb groups (AC9E2LA07). They have not yet examined the different types of verbs — doing, saying, sensing, relating — and how each represents a distinct kind of process.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students understand how verbs represent different processes: doing, feeling, thinking, saying and relating.

nodes.label: Doing and saying verbs
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify doing verbs (action) and saying verbs in narrative texts and explain what each type tells the reader.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two doing verbs and one saying verb in a narrative text and explain what each type of verb tells the reader.
nodes.typical_width: Explore doing and saying verbs in narrative texts, understanding how doing verbs show action and saying verbs indicate how characters speak — and how the choice of saying verb (e.g. 'whispered', 'shouted') adds information.
wider: Compare the doing verbs in an action sequence versus a description in the same narrative, discussing what the verb type choices reveal about the pacing
Explore how different saying verbs in dialogue change the reader's interpretation of the character's emotion or intention
success_criteria: Student identifies a doing verb and a saying verb, naming the type of each
Student explains what information each verb type provides — beyond just 'it's an action'

nodes.label: Sensing and relating verbs
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify sensing verbs (feeling, thinking, perceiving) and relating verbs (defining, describing) and explain how they construct meaning differently from doing verbs.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one sensing verb and one relating verb in a text and explain what type of process each represents.
nodes.typical_width: Explore sensing verbs (feeling, thinking, perceiving) and relating verbs (constructing definitions and descriptions) — identifying different types and explaining how they control meaning in a clause differently from doing verbs.
wider: Find sensing verbs in a narrative text and discuss how they let readers understand what characters are thinking and feeling without being told directly
Compare a description written with relating verbs versus adjectives and discuss what each choice achieves

response_modes.reason: Sensing and relating verbs don't look like 'typical verbs' to students. Seeing them in multiple different text contexts — narrative, information, description — helps students recognise the full range of what verbs can do beyond physical action.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The verb type framework (doing/saying/sensing/relating) is a rich analytical tool for both reading and writing at Y3. Understanding that 'felt', 'believed' and 'seemed' are all verbs with specific process types expands students' grammatical repertoire meaningfully.
success_criteria: Student identifies a sensing or relating verb and names its process type
Student explains how the sensing or relating verb contributes differently to meaning than a doing verb would
